guideline: Annotators assessed overall quality on a 1-5 Likert scale (coherence and relevance without copying), indicated if implications made headlines more or less trustworthy, rated viewpoint (majority or minority), and indicated social acceptability.

Annotators rate overall quality (coherence, relevance) on a 1‑5 Likert scale, rate trustworthiness before and after seeing the implication, and indicate social acceptability / majority vs. minority viewpoint.

We ask the annotators to assess the overall quality of generated implications on a 1-5 Likert scale (i.e. whether they are coherent and relevant to the headline without directly copying). We measure whether generated implications impact readers' perception of news reliability by asking annotators whether a generated implication makes them perceive the news headline as more (+) or less (-) trustworthy. We ask annotators to rate their perception of the beliefs invoked by an implication in terms of whether they represent a majority (mainstream) or minority (fringe) viewpoint.
